You can use narrative tenses when you want to tell a story.

When you want to talk about situations that happened at a certain time in the past or you want to tell a story, you can use the Simple Past, Past Continuous and Past Perfect verb tenses. These tenses are the most common narrative tenses and each has a different use and meaning.
The Simple Past is used for:
  • completed actions in the past, this is used with definite times in the past
I brushed my teeth, got dressed, and left the house.

• past habits
I went to ballet classes every evening when I was a child.

You can also express past habits with used to or would
  • used to:
    • for habits that happened in the past but not anymore
    • this cannot be used with actions that only happened once
    • can be used with both states and actions
She used to bake cookies every Friday.
She used to like eating dark chocolate.

• would:
    • used for past habits but not used for past states
She would bake cookies every Friday.
She would enjoy eating dark chocolate.

You can use the Past Continuous for:
  • background actions
When I left home that night it was snowing.

• an action that was happening at a time in the past
I was eating dinner at 6 o'clock last night.

• interrupted actions
Lara was taking a shower when the phone rang.

• unfinished actions
I was reading a book last night. (the book isn't finished)

• repeated actions (usually something that we found annoying, used with “always”)
He was always forgetting his keys and getting locked out of the apartment.

• temporary situations
Roberto moves a lot because of his job. He was living in Germany last month.

You can use the Past Perfect to:
  • show that an action happened before another in the past
I didn't eat anything for dinner because I had eaten a late lunch.

• add style and variety in a narrative
I took a shower, watched a movie, and went to bed.
I went to bed after I had taken a shower and watched a movie.
Both sentences above are correct. Instead of expressing everything in the Simple Past, you can add variety to your sentences by using the Past Perfect as well.
You can talk about surprising or unexpected situations by using concession clauses.
You can use a concession clause to express something that is the opposite of the idea in the main clause. It can be something surprising or unexpected based on what you know of the main clause.

For example:
Although she was afraid of snakes, she held one around her neck for a picture.
It is unexpected that this person would want to hold a snake because she is afraid of them.

You can use other words to express concession. You can use:
although
though
even though
even if
no matter (followed by a wh- question word)
however (despite anything to the contrary)
whatever (no matter what, used sometimes)
as (when the structure is adjective + as + be)

Examples:
Although/ Though/ Even though the trains were delayed, everyone managed to get to work on time.

Even if I knew how to speak French, I wouldn't want to visit France.

No matter how hungry I am, I will never eat my sister's cooking.

However difficult your life may be, there is always someone out there with more problems.

Whatever his intentions may have been, he greeted us as friends.

Rich as he was, he hardly spent any money.

images.text:
Today's activists are an eclectic bunch. Though a lot of activists are famous people with money, anyone who has a passion and the drive to help others may become an activist. It is not only famous artists who become involved in activism.
Darius Weems is restricted to a wheelchair and has had Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy since he was five. Because he had lost his brother to the same disease he decided to raise awareness about the disease. He had the idea to make a documentary about DMD. Although he had not succeeded in getting his wish of having his wheelchair “jazzed up”, he made a journey from Georgia to California in it. The film “Darius Goes West: The Roll of His Life” raised 1.5 million dollars for DMD research.
Christopher Yao is another young activist who started Kids Change the World. This organization provides free educational tools and medical help. Christopher's organization inspired 15,000 students to become leaders in their communities. The organization helps educate various medical facilities.

However you become an activist doesn't matter. Another activist known around the world is Angelina Jolie. When Jolie was filming Tomb Raider in Cambodia in 2001, her eyes were opened to the world around her. She had been to The Office of The United Nations High Commissioner of Refugees when she started the Jolie-Pitt foundation. The foundation then donated one million dollars to Doctors Without Borders which was created by doctors and journalists in 1971 to help the less fortunate with malnutrition, control epidemics and help victims of natural disasters.

In 1997, Malala Yousafzi was born in Mingova, Pakistan. She was attending the school her father founded when an obstacle arose. Even though the Taliban tried to take control and threatened to deny Malala and other girls an education, Malala persevered. In 2009 she began a blog for the BBC about her experiences which gained public attention. In 2013 she was nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize and the next year she won.
Even if you don't have the financial means to become an activist, you can create an organization that gets people involved in the many issues that exist.
